a0009 recalls the ratios. a0008 says the ratios are used for two-dimensional right-angled-triangle problems, which include the elevation and depression ones.
a0026 (WE1) and a0028 (WE3) both make 'identify the opposite and adjacent sides and the hypotenuse' an explicit first step. That is the src labelling skill.
a0027 (WE2) reads which sides are given ('hypotenuse and opposite') and picks sin from that. This uses side labelling as a step, though only implicitly.

a0026 (WE1) and a0028 (WE3) choose the ratio, write it as opposite/hypotenuse or similar, rearrange and calculate. That is the src method. dst is a close restatement of src, but the text does use the method.

a0028 (WE3) finds a building height by choosing tan, rearranging and solving for the side. That is the src method inside an elevation problem. The a0035 exercise quote is present, but WE3 is what shows the reliance.

a0027 (WE2) uses sin of the known sides and then the inverse to get the angle. The a0033 and a0034 exercises ask for an angle of elevation from two known lengths, which needs the same inverse-ratio method.

a0011 says the ratios and the theorem of Pythagoras are used together. a0026 (WE1) says the third side can also be found with Pythagoras. The dst objective itself names Pythagoras, and src includes it.
a0027 (WE2) contains the step 'Use the theorem of Pythagoras to determine' BE, which feeds the cosine-inverse step. That is the Pythagoras part of src used as a step.

It does not name 'alternate angles', so the reliance is implicit, but it is clearly the step in use.
